column1: # PROVENANCE of the pre-push files this repo VENDORS from omnibase_infra
# (OMN-17435). Read by tests/scripts/test_prepush_host_table.py.
# WHY VENDORED AND NOT SHARED -- the decision, on the facts, not on preference:
#   * A sibling-clone source (`. "$OMNI_HOME/omnibase_infra/scripts/hooks/..."`)
#     makes a FAIL-CLOSED gate depend on a second repository being checked out
#     next to this one. An isolated single-repo clone, a CI runner checkout, or
#     a contributor without the whole workspace would then hit `die` on every
#     heavy push. A placement optimisation must not be able to brick a push.
#   * A pip-installed picker moves the gate behind a synced `.venv`, which a
#     pre-push hook cannot assume exists -- and the hook must run BEFORE the
#     machinery that would install it.
#   * A git submodule has the same failure shape as the sibling clone, one
#     `git clone` flag away (`--recurse-submodules` omitted -> empty dir).
# So the copy is local, and the DRIFT is what gets mechanically controlled:
# each file's sha256 is pinned, and the upstream revision it was taken from is
# recorded HERE so "has upstream moved?" is answerable by anyone with network
# access, without this repo depending on that access at push time.
# WHAT THIS FILE ADDS OVER A BARE DIGEST PIN (the OMN-17159 shape): a digest
# alone detects a LOCAL edit. It cannot tell you the copy is STALE. Measured
# 2026-09-01, that is not hypothetical: omnibase_core's OMN-17159 copy pins
# 067706bb...c096 = omnibase_infra commit 81955c0d0 (OMN-17269), while
# omnibase_infra dev already shipped 3e1c975b0 (OMN-17392, memory-aware
# admission + prefer_remote + bounded off-box wait) as ba56bd0d...9f88. Core's
# vendored copy was a full feature behind before its own PR merged. This repo
# therefore vendors the CURRENT tip and records which commit that was.
# TO UPDATE: re-copy the file from the named upstream path, update BOTH the
# sha256 and the upstream_commit here in the same commit, re-run
# tests/scripts/test_prepush_host_table.py, and name the upstream revision in
# the PR body. Editing a vendored file WITHOUT touching this record is the
# thing that cannot happen quietly.
# 2026-09-02, OMN-17606 -- THIS COPY CARRIES A FIX THAT IS LANDING UPSTREAM IN
# PARALLEL, and the row below records that rather than hiding it. Three measured
# defects in the shared slot probe made `slots>1` placement inert fleet-wide,
# and on a `slot_mode=queue` row with an EXISTING BUT EMPTY QUEUE file they also
# made the placement-time stacking guard FAIL-OPEN (an empty `grep -c .` prints
# 0 AND exits 1, so `|| echo 0` fired too, `q` became two words, and every later
# field was read shifted). omnimarket is hit by two of the three on every push
# -- the leg double-count applies to every host in every repo, and the field
# shift applies to h201, this table's only queue row -- so the fix is applied
# here in the same pass as omnibase_infra's rather than a merge cycle behind it.
# The recorded commit is therefore the BASE this copy was taken from
# (omnibase_infra dev @ c1c9ef19e, whose file digest is the previously pinned
# e5b849169a5e...fc4e); the bytes below are that file PLUS the four-change
# OMN-17606 delta, which is landing upstream in parallel on the branch
# `jonah/omn-17606-slot-probe-correctness`. A digest check of this row against
# the recorded commit will therefore MISMATCH, deliberately and visibly, until
# the re-sync below; the digest still does its own job, which is detecting a
# local edit to the shipped file. The bytes also differ from omnibase_infra's
# own fixed copy by FOUR COMMENT LINES ONLY: upstream's wording names a
# vendoring repo by name, which this repo's
# test_the_picker_library_is_not_edited_into_a_repo_specific_fork forbids inside
# the shared library, so the same sentence is written repo-neutrally here.
# RE-SYNC CONDITION: when omnibase_infra's OMN-17606 fix merges to dev,
# re-copy the file, update this record, and re-run
# tests/scripts/test_prepush_host_table.py. If the upstream wording still names
# a repo at that point, the fork guard is the authority -- raise it upstream,
# never silence the guard to make the digests match.
#path
# 2026-09-03, OMN-17564 -- SECOND parallel-landing delta on this same file, on
# top of the OMN-17606 one recorded above. The remote execution leg shipped the
# SELECTION across the seam and dropped the EXECUTION POLICY: every dispatched
# heavy suite ran single-threaded with no per-test watchdog, and the execution
# ssh carried ConnectTimeout only -- which governs the handshake, so a host that
# wedged AFTER connect held the lane forever (measured: 5h29m, zero bytes, no
# marker). Both faces are in this file, so the fix is vendored here in the same
# pass rather than a merge cycle behind upstream.
# The recorded commit is upstream's OMN-17564 BRANCH commit
# (jonah/omn-17564-prepush-remote-leg-policy @ d9f76efd6, itself rebased on
# omnibase_infra dev @ 77ffa91c9), NOT a dev commit -- upstream's push is
# blocked on lab host saturation, not on review, so recording the branch it is
# proven on is the honest available provenance. This repo therefore now carries
# TWO deltas ahead of upstream dev; the digest below is this file's own, and it
# still does its real job, which is detecting a LOCAL edit to the shipped file.
# Bytes differ from upstream's OMN-17564 copy by the OMN-17606 slot-probe block
# recorded above PLUS THREE COMMENT PASSAGES ONLY: upstream's wording names
# `omnibase_core` three times (as the repo whose local heavy leg already runs
# `-n4`, and as the source of the 3h48m55s worst-case measurement) and asserts
# `.github/workflows/ci.yml test-parallel` as "this repo's own CI". Both are
# false-or-forbidden here -- `test_the_picker_library_is_not_edited_into_a_repo
# _specific_fork` forbids the repo name inside the shared library, and THIS
# repo's ci.yml has no test-parallel job at all -- so the same facts are stated
# repo-neutrally. No executable line differs.
# RE-SYNC CONDITION: when omnibase_infra's OMN-17606 and OMN-17564 fixes both
# merge to dev, re-copy the file, collapse both notes into one record, and
# re-run tests/scripts/test_prepush_host_table.py plus
# tests/scripts/test_prepush_remote_leg_policy.py. If upstream's wording still
# names a repo, the fork guard is the authority -- raise it upstream, never
# silence the guard to make the digests match.
scripts/hooks/prepush_dispatch.sh
scripts/hooks/prepush_override_grant.py
scripts/hooks/pytest_full_suite_host_guard.py
